evan: heads up — hitting a reproducible throughput cliff when enabling FP8 on H100 with TE fused kernels. Batch 4-8 @ seq_len 1024, p50 OK but p95/p99 and throughput drop ~30%. tail latency spikes. attaching quick trace below
maria: can you paste the kernel selector dump and the TE flags you used?
evans: selector dump snippet:
```
kernel_choice: fused_fp8_dot_mha (chosen)
fallback_path: nvrtc_slowpath_dot
est_cycles: 1.2e6
measured_cycles: 3.9e6 (first 5 iters)
te_flags: --use-fused-fp8 --workspace=auto --te-kernel=best
```
evan: note: we see an nvrtc compile happening in the trace right when the model hits the 1st big request, which correlates with the first big tail spike. after compile subsequent iters still slower than fp16.
jon: nvrtc compile on demand will definitely blow up cold-starts, but 30% steady drop after warmup sounds like something else (regspill / memcopy). can you capture smem/regs/occupancy for the fused kernel?
sasha: adding that — also observed weird KV behavior in the same run: cache miss rate jumps after ~600 tokens and we see small tensor copies labeled "kv_repack". might be allocator churn with workspace=auto trying to steal ephemeral buffers.
perf-bot: snapshot: fp16 baseline p99=620ms, fused-fp8 run p99=1150ms, throughput 70% of baseline. memory transient spikes + 3x host-device memcpy events.
maria: hypothesis: TE fused FP8 kernel increases register pressure and causes spilling to local memory on H100 for these matmul shapes, also workspace=auto triggers allocator migration that causes extra copies. two things to try: force TE workspace prealloc and try the compat kernel (`--te-kernel=compat`) which is lower fusion but better register usage.
evans: tried `--workspace=prealloc` and pinned `--te-kernel=compat`; tail improves but peak throughput drops a bit vs auto. also tried `--batch-pacing=linear` which reduced jitter but further lowered peak throughput ~6%.
jon: another angle — selector cost model may be undercounting quant/dequant overheads. for some cross-layer matmuls we actually hit INT8/compat shim because scale clipping was flagged during calibration, so cost model chose a different path that forces extra conversions. we should log which matmuls are getting int8-compat fallback and why.
sasha: i captured a tiny log: `quant_scale_clip=true` for layer 23, then selector switched to `int8-compat` for subsequent layers. looks like calibration drift on long prompts triggers clipping. we should add a calibration run that exercises long-tail prompts.
maria: agreed. actions: 1) add TE precompile step in startup to avoid nvrtc at runtime (evan), 2) tweak selector cost weights for dequant/conv overhead (maria), 3) add KV allocator metrics and a diagnostic flag to force prealloc (sasha), 4) add long-tail calibration evaluation to CI (jon).
evans: i've started a local branch with TE precompile patch and a flag `--te-precompile=all` — initial results: removes first-iter compile spike but overall perf still 10-20% below fp16 on shapes we care about. digging into PTX regs next.
jon: can you run `nvprof --occupancy` on the fused kernel and dump register usage? if regs>200 we will spill. also check L2 writeback counts.
sasha: i'll wire a small allocator metric set that reports `kv_miss_rate`, `kv_repack_count`, and `workspace_migrations` to console for next run. should make it easier to correlate.
maria: small experimental idea: add a selector policy that simulates the runtime memory pressure (workspace fragmentation) when scoring kernel candidates. might avoid picking kernels that do extra copies.
evans: good call. for now i'm going to revert to `compat` for the perf tests and run a reg instrument to capture PTX register usage. will post logs here.
maria: thanks — tagging infra for flamegraph access: @jon @sasha. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: queued a nightly job: `fp8-h100-longseq-calib` with `--te-precompile`, `--workspace=prealloc`, and long-tail prompt set. results will post in #eng-runtime tomorrow.
